title: WOTS PRF midstate-resume: compute the two per-layer SHA-256 midstates once per sign, resume per call (byte-identical output, no address re-base)
threat: 44,118 wots_secret calls per sign each push the raw 32-byte sk_seed through the HASH peripheral's DIN at the same intra-call offset — the horizontal/template residual of archive §18 and the exact 'SK.seed reused across thousands of PRF calls' pattern of Kannwischer 2018 / Saarinen 2024. #229 assumed closing this requires re-basing every key (invariant #6).
proposal: Because block 1 of wots_secret is sk_seed||"wots"||to_b4(layer)||tree_b32[0..24] and tree_b32[0..24] is always zero (u64 right-aligned in 32 B), the chaining value after block 1 is a constant per (sk_seed, layer). Compute the two midstates (layer 0, layer 1) once per sign (or once per SLOT_CACHE keygen) and run only block 2 per call, either (a) via the HASH peripheral's context-swap registers (HASH_CSRx suspend/resume, RM0456 §HASH 'context swapping') or (b) via `sha2::compress256` in software for the 64-byte second block with explicit padding. Outputs are bit-identical to the current `sha256(...)`, so pubkeys, CREATE2 addresses, the on-chain verifier and all test vectors are untouched; pin with a differential test against the existing wots_secret. Store the midstates as ZeroizeOnDrop in the SigningKey cache. Side effect: ~44k fewer compressions per sign (~8% of the 539,616 hashes).
rationale: Reduces sk_seed-absorbing compressions from 44,118+26,636 to 26,636 (FORS only) + 2 without any wire/derivation change, closing the WOTS half of #229 pre- AND post-launch. Honest limit: block-2 compressions still combine a secret chaining value with varying known input, so the vertical-DPA exposure on the midstate (which suffices to forge WOTS for that layer; layer-1 WOTS alone is a full forgery) is UNCHANGED — this item removes the horizontal/template surface on sk_seed itself, which is the key shared with FORS and grind_r. FORS cannot be restructured this way (single block, secret and varying input mixed).
repo_evidence: sphincs-c10/src/hash.rs:376-392 (wots_secret update order: sk_seed, "wots", layer, tree_b32, kp, chain_idx)
sphincs-c10/src/hash.rs:106-125 (hw-sha256 hook: init/update/final only — no midstate API)
hw/src/hash.rs (no CSR/context-swap usage: grep CSR -> only DHCSR)
issue #229 (states the restructure 'violates launch invariant #6' — not true for WOTS as the layout already isolates the secret in block 1)
vendor_precedent: none for SLH-DSA on a wallet; conceptually Fluhrer's 'PRF tree' (NIST PQC 2024) and HMAC's precomputed ipad/opad midstates.
risks: If (b) is chosen, one secret-CV compression per call moves from the HASH peripheral to the CPU, where Lecomte 2026 SASCA applies — prefer (a) and validate HASH CSR semantics on U585 (CSR count differs per HASH revision). The midstate is a new long-lived secret in SRAM (same class as sk_seed). Double-compute/F-16 shuffle interaction: both passes must use the same midstates. Must re-run hash_counts.rs expectations (≥60,000 lower bound would fall to ~26,638 secret calls — update the test, do not weaken the census).
